extracted.intended_audience: Owners/operators of facilities and suppliers required to report greenhouse gas emissions under 40 CFR part 98; environmental compliance officers, environmental consultants, and legal counsel advising regulated entities
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule amending 40 CFR part 98 to extend the annual greenhouse gas (GHG) reporting deadline for reporting year 2025 and to explain applicability, procedures, and statutory determinations associated with that extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: RY2025 reporting deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual GHG report for reporting year 2025 must be submitted no later than October 30, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies only to reporting year 2025; EPA amended §98.3(b) to add this paragraph. EPA states the extension will allow time to consider comments on the GHGRP Reconsideration Proposal and to take any final actions before the revised deadline, and to allow entities to benefit from any burden reduction revisions or to prepare and submit RY2025 reports. This action is final and effective February 27, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: General annual reporting schedule (standard deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual report for reporting years 2011 and beyond must be submitted no later than March 31 of each calendar year for GHG emissions in the previous calendar year, except as provided in paragraphs (b)(1), (5), and (6) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the default schedule for §98.3(b). The rule also provides that if the final day of any time period falls on a weekend or Federal holiday, the time period is extended to the next business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: RY2024 reporting deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual GHG report for reporting year 2024 must be submitted no later than May 30, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified as paragraph (b)(5) in §98.3(b). Included as an exception to the standard March 31 deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability / regulated entities
rubrics_metrics.description: This final regulation affects entities that submit annual GHG reports pursuant to the GHGRP (40 CFR part 98). Entities affected by this action are owners or operators of facilities that are direct emitters or suppliers of GHGs or that sequester carbon dioxide (CO2) gas underground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1 provides examples of affected entities by NAICS category (e.g., electricity generation, petroleum refineries, chemical manufacturers, landfills, sequestration projects). Table 1 is not exhaustive; other types of entities may also be subject. If unsure about applicability to a particular facility, consult the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT section or the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting threshold (who must report)
rubrics_metrics.description: The GHGRP applies primarily to large facilities emitting at least 25,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalents (MTCO2e), upstream suppliers of fossil fuels and industrial GHGs, and industries that capture and sequester CO2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximately 8,200 facilities, suppliers, and CO2 injection sites submit data annually. Applicability depends on source category and statutory provisions in CAA sections cited in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specified methodologies and electronic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities calculate emissions using methodologies that are specified under the regulations and report data to the EPA using the electronic Greenhouse Gas Reporting Tool (e-GGRT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA may prepare and release the e-GGRT system in advance of the revised RY2025 reporting deadline to give facilities time to work in the system. Methodologies are those specified in 40 CFR part 98 and supporting materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and error-correction process
rubrics_metrics.description: Once data are submitted, the EPA conducts a multi-step verification process to ensure reported data are accurate, complete, and consistent. If the EPA identifies potential errors, it will notify the reporter, who can resolve the issue either by providing an acceptable response describing why the flagged issue is not an error or by correcting the flagged issue and resubmitting their annual GHG report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported data are made available to the public typically seven to eight months after the reporting deadline through EPA tools and factsheets. Entities should be prepared to respond to flags or to correct and resubmit data when notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate effectiveness and APA §553(d)(1) exception
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule is effective immediately upon publication. Section 553(d)(1) provides that final rules shall not become effective until 30 days after publication except a substantive rule which grants or recognizes an exemption or relieves a restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA determined that extending the reporting deadline relieves a restriction and thus does not require the normal 30-day delay. The preamble cites case law supporting immediate effectiveness when the action relieves obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation of the final action
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule changes only the reporting deadline for annual greenhouse gas (GHG) reports for reporting year 2025 in response to comments received on the proposed rescission of the GHGRP; EPA anticipates addressing the remainder of the proposed rule in one or more subsequent final actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule does not finalize other proposed rescissions or revisions to GHGRP obligations; those will be considered separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket and public access to materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA established a docket for this action under Docket Id. No. EPA-HQ-OAR-2025-0186. All documents in the docket are listed in the www.regulations.gov index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some docket materials may not be publicly available (e.g., CBI) or may only be available in hard copy at the EPA Docket Center; the public reading room has specified hours and telephone numbers. A brief summary is available at regulations.gov and the final rule will be posted to the EPA GHGRP website after signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review and limitations on objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicial review of this final action is available only by filing a petition for review in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit by April 28, 2026. Under CAA section 307(d)(7)(B), only an objection to a rule or procedure which was raised with reasonable specificity during the period for public comment may be raised during judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAA section 307(d) procedures apply. EPA provides a mechanism for reconsideration if an objection could not practicably be raised during the comment period or arose after comments but within the time for judicial review; such objections should be submitted as a Petition for Reconsideration to the Administrator with copies to the contacts listed in the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) determination
rubrics_metrics.description: This action does not impose any new information collection burden under the PRA. OMB has previously approved the information collection requirements contained in the existing regulation and has assigned OMB control numbers 2060-0629, 2060-0748, and 2060-0751.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The action merely extends the deadline for submitting annual GHG reports for reporting year 2025 data from March 31, 2026, to October 30, 2026, and does not create new PRA obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) certification
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA certifies that this final action will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the RFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's rationale is that the action imposes no net regulatory burden because it confirms an extension of a compliance date and does not change other regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates and Executive Order determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA determined that: (a) this action does not contain an unfunded mandate as described in UMRA; (b) this action is not a significant regulatory action under EO12866 and thus was not submitted to OMB for review; (c) this action is considered an Executive Order 14192 deregulation; (d) it has no federalism implications (EO13132) or Tribal implications (EO13175); (e) it is not subject to EO13045 or EO13211; and (f) it does not involve technical standards (NTTAA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA notes that the action is subject to the Congressional Review Act but is not a 'major rule' as defined by 5 U.S.C. 804(2). These determinations describe the statutory and executive-order review posture of the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special scheduling exceptions and provisions for new or changed facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (b)(1) and paragraphs (b)(2)-(b)(4) provide special scheduling rules: certain subparts and suppliers had different deadlines (e.g., reporting year 2011 facilities listed in (b)(1) had a September 28, 2012 deadline), new facilities beginning operation report from first operating month through December 31 of that year, and facilities becoming subject due to physical or operational change follow specified reporting conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions (b)(1)-(b)(4) describe transitional and special-case reporting schedules and notification requirements (e.g., notifying EPA by March 31, 2012, for certain second reports in 2012). They remain part of §98.3(b) alongside the standard schedule and RY2024/RY2025 exceptions.
